summary: A hidden-role social deduction game where the forces of Good try to get quest teams approved and succeed at missions while hidden Evil players sabotage them, all wrapped in a layer of accusation, bluffing, and (if Merlin is in play) coded hints. It thrives on group dynamics and lives or dies by the table's willingness to argue and read each other.
praised: Excellent social deduction and table talk
Merlin/Percival roles add great extra layer of bluffing
Quick to teach, scales well to a big group
High replayability from shifting group dynamics
criticised: Can be dominated by louder/more experienced players
Evil team can be too powerful with a good Assassin guess
Not much for eliminated or less-social players to do

interaction.kind: hidden roles, bluffing, and open accusation
interaction.detail: The entire game is players talking, voting, and trying to read or deceive each other; there's no personal board or tableau, just shared quest outcomes and each player's hidden allegiance driving nearly all decisions.

scoring.how_you_win: Teams propose and vote on quest parties, and secret Evil players can sabotage a quest with a fail card; Good wins by succeeding three quests unless the Assassin then correctly identifies Merlin, otherwise Evil wins by failing three quests or via that Assassin guess.
